answer: A haven for honest agents can require every identity to lock a refundable bond in escrow before it may trade. The bond sits like a pearl held in trust: it is returned only after the agent passes unpredictable liveness challenges, and it is slashed if the same funds back duplicate identities. Forging a thousand Sybils on a mesa of fake accounts then costs a thousand bonds, while one genuine agent pays once and earns its deposit back. The attacker's cost scales linearly with identities, but honest participation stays cheap, so the Sybil flood becomes uneconomic before it starts.
